picks.title: Audacity 4 Is Finally Here: The Biggest Update in the Editor's History
picks.excerpt: Audacity 4 ships a redesigned clip workflow, Workspaces and a full visual overhaul — and keeps the Intel OpenVINO AI toolset (music separation, noise suppression, transcription, music generation) plus new AI-powered podcast features inside a free, open-source editor.
picks.rationale: The biggest rewrite in Audacity's history puts stem separation, noise suppression and transcription behind a modern clip workflow for free — the lowest-cost AI audio bench anyone can install tomorrow.

picks.title: Producely Dialr: This Plugin Controller Maps with AI!
picks.excerpt: First shown at Superbooth25, the Producely Dialr hardware controller is now orderable: an AI-assisted mapping engine reads whatever plugin is in focus and assigns its most useful parameters to the knobs automatically, removing the MIDI-learn step from hands-on mixing and sound design.
picks.rationale: AI applied to the boring part instead of the music — the controller reads the focused plugin and maps its knobs itself, deleting MIDI-learn from every session.

picks.title: Creating plugins in Suno Studio 2.0
picks.excerpt: Suno's own walkthrough of building custom audio plugins from the chat bar inside Studio 2.0 — the vendor showing how a prompt becomes a signal-processing device in a working session.
picks.rationale: Suno moves from generating songs to generating the processors that shape them: a prompt in the chat bar becomes a working plugin, shown step by step by the vendor.

picks.title: Armin van Buuren and Laidback Luke join 'responsible' AI music company Moises as advisors
picks.excerpt: Two headline DJ-producers have signed on as advisors to Moises, whose stem-separation, AI mixing/mastering and generative session-player tools are trained only on licensed and authorised content. The pair will steer how the toolset is shaped for working producers.
picks.rationale: The licensed-training-data camp gets two working producers steering the roadmap — the clearest signal yet of where Moises' stem and session-player tools are heading.

picks.title: Alok fans get personalised music video with headphone purchases
picks.excerpt: Alok and agency Rise New York & Partners turned a headphone purchase into an AI-generated music video that is unique for every buyer — a production pipeline where the 'one video per release' assumption is replaced by per-fan rendering.
picks.rationale: Kills the 'one video per release' assumption: a shipped campaign where every buyer gets a distinct AI-rendered music video, and the pipeline is the deliverable.
